## Community Meeting Answers Questions for More Than 100 Participants as They Prepare to Submit Claims to SCE’s Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program


Nov. 12 in-person session in Pasadena provides another opportunity to learn more ahead of Nov. 30 submission deadline, with more than 17,600 participants already submitting claims.


November 6, 2026


[Media Relations](https://newsroom.edison.com/) : 626-302-2255,[\[email protected\]](https://newsroom.edison.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#a4cac1d3d7e4d7c7c18ac7cbc9)
[Investor Relations](https://www.edison.com/home/investors.html) : Sam Ramraj, 626-302-2540
Feinberg/Biros: Amy Weiss, 202-203-0448,[\[email protected\]](https://newsroom.edison.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#4a2b27330a3d2f2339393a3f282623292b2c2c2b23383964292527)


ROSEMEAD, Calif., Nov. 6, 2026 — With the Nov. 30 deadline approaching to submit a claim to Southern California Edison’s[Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program](https://sce.com/directclaims) , SCE is continuing to provide opportunities for community members impacted by the Eaton Fire to learn about the program, ask questions and get help submitting a claim.


More than 100 participants attended last week’s virtual community meeting. An in-person meeting on Thurs., Nov. 12 in Pasadena will provide another opportunity for community members to get their questions answered and connect with resources as they consider whether to submit a claim.


“We’re committed to providing clear information and direct answers to help community members understand their options,” said Pedro J. Pizarro, president and CEO of Edison International, SCE’s parent company. “We encourage those impacted by the Eaton Fire to submit a claim by November 30 to learn what compensation may be available to them.”


As of Nov. 6, 2026:


- More than 5,730 claims submitted, consisting of over 17,600 individuals, trusts and legal entities, with 42% submitted by attorneys or authorized representatives.
- More than 3,320 offers extended to nearly 8,200 claimants, totaling more than $1.1 billion. More than 80% of offers have been accepted, with more pending. Only about 2% of offers have been declined.
- More than 4,600 claimants paid, totaling nearly $660 million, with many more in process.


**Community Questions Take Center Stage**


At last week’s virtual meeting, more than 100 participants asked about pursuing Eaton Fire compensation through SCE’s program. Key questions included:


**How does the program compare with compensation through litigation?** The Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program is designed to provide compensation in line with settlement values for similar claims in past wildfire lawsuits through a more streamlined and faster approach, with offers and payments measured in weeks or months rather than years. The March 8, 2027, initial trial date should not be viewed as a timeline for receiving compensation through litigation. Only eight households have been selected by the court to participate in the initial trial, and broader resolution through litigation will take longer.


Submitting a claim through SCE’s program takes about two hours, results in a no-commitment offer and preserves the option to pursue litigation.


**How is compensation calculated?** Compensation is based on a combination of applicable categories, including economic loss (for property damage, business interruption and physical injury), non-economic loss (for personal impacts), a[Direct Claim Premium](https://energized.edison.com/wildfire-recovery-compensation-program/faq#directclaimpremium) (for participating in the program) and compensation for legal expenses (for those represented by counsel). Learn more about[how payments are calculated](https://energized.edison.com/wildfire-recovery-compensation-program/faq#calculatedpayments) and[see sample offers](https://energized.edison.com/wildfire-recovery-compensation-program#sample-offers-section) .


**How does insurance impact compensation?** If insurance is available, that amount is deducted from certain compensation categories and the overall offer from the program. A lack of insurance does not prevent an otherwise eligible claimant from submitting a claim. Community members are encouraged to submit a claim by Nov. 30 to learn what compensation may be available to them.


**How long does the process take?** On average, offers are being delivered within 36 days after submission of a substantially complete claim. Claims submitted by Nov. 30 will continue to be reviewed and processed afterward, even if validation or preparation of an offer has not been completed. Submitting a claim, receiving an offer and evaluating that offer do not waive a claimant’s rights. Payments are made within 30 days after all settlement conditions are satisfied, with many claimants receiving payment in two to three weeks.


**Nov. 12 Community Meeting in Pasadena**


The next community meeting will be held at Westminster Presbyterian Church in Pasadena on Thurs., Nov. 12, at 6 p.m. Community members can learn more, ask questions and connect with resources to support rebuilding and recovery. Neighborhood Housing Services of Los Angeles County will have case managers at the event to provide guidance on housing, rebuilding and recovery, including loan, grant and financing programs. Lori R. Gay, president and chief executive officer of Neighborhood Housing Services of Los Angeles County, will share her experience. The panel will also include an independent attorney to offer an outside legal perspective.


[Register here](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=7o8qW5VM3EuKrhlviqyxtvm2QhUxtzRBjstH6wODNZhUMkpBOVdWQVc3UVBJUTlYNEpUOUJJTDU3Ri4u&route=shorturl) for this session and the additional virtual community meeting on Thurs., Nov. 19.


**Submit a Claim by Nov. 30**


To submit a claim and access detailed guidance in English and Spanish, visit the[Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program web page](https://www.sce.com/directclaims) . One-on-one assistance is available in multiple languages by phone or in person, from start to finish. Call 888-912-8528 to get started.


**About Southern California Edison**


An Edison International (NYSE: EIX) company, Southern California Edison is one of the nation’s largest electric utilities, serving a population of approximately 15 million via 5 million customer accounts in a 50,000-square-mile service area within Central, Coastal and Southern California.
